idiom_name: errgroup.WithContext + g.Go/g.Wait, context cancellation for the whole group
implementation_notes: Go's structured idiom is x/sync/errgroup: WithContext derives a context that is cancelled the first time a child returns an error or when Wait returns, so every child receives that ctx and watches ctx.Done() to cooperate with cancellation; Wait joins all children and returns the first non-nil error. sync.WaitGroup is the stdlib floor - it tracks lifetime but propagates neither errors nor cancellation - and bare go statements outside any group are the escape hatch the pattern exists to replace. Bound fan-out with g.SetLimit or a semaphore.
pitfalls: Wait waits for the goroutines, not for cancellation: a child that ignores ctx keeps the group alive, so the signal has to be checked at safe points.
A panic inside g.Go is not converted into the group's error (the implementation deliberately lets panics crash the process), so recover inside the child when containment is required.
Children started with a bare go statement are invisible to Wait and leak past the parent operation.
The derived context is cancelled by the first failure, but children that already returned keep their side effects - idempotency and cleanup stay the application's job.
